contributorNote: Compiled from 'An Introduction to the Ateso Language' by J.H. Hilders and J.C.D. Lawrence (Eagle Press / East African Literature Bureau, 1957). Ateso is an Eastern Nilotic language of the Teso-Turkana group, spoken primarily in Busia County (Teso North and Teso South sub-counties), Kenya, and widely across Eastern Uganda (Soroti, Kumi, Ngora, Bukedea, Katakwi, Amuria, Tororo). Thoroughly analyzed and structured with accurate grammatical gender (masculine e-, feminine a-, diminutive i-), plural noun classes, and verbal classes (ko- and ki-).
